records.deidentified_narrative: the little elm police department accident investigation/reconstruction team findings in this incident are as follows. the team for this case is comprised of the following individuals; inv. sean kinney, inv. curt slocumb, cpl. james loney and sgt. jay compton. the accident investigation/reconstruction team is very familiar with working accidents on this bridge in inclement weather conditions. the bridge is known to ice over before the roadway, as was the case on the morning of this crash (there was a layer of ice built up on the bridge). the weather conditions at the time of the crash were as follows: the temperature was approximately 28 degrees, and the wind was out of the north at approximately 14 mph (wind chill 16. 9 degrees). [roadway] conditions on the bridge and lack of artificial illumination were the underlying causes of the crash. according to statistical data, sunrise did not occur until 07:31 am on the morning of the crash, and there are no artificial lights illuminating the roadway where the crash occurred. no speed calculations were able to be computed due to lack of post and pre-impact skid marks due to ice on the roadway. the victim [person] [medical facility] prior to our arrival on scene, however photographs of the victim yielded the following information. [person] wearing a dark colored jacket (black), dark pants (navy), dark boots (black/gray), and gloves (green/gray/black) and a light blue shirt at the time of the crash. on the morning of january 1st, 2018 inv. sean kinney, inv. curt slocumb, cpl. james loney and sgt. stoney ward visited lw`s towing to look at the vehicles that were towed from the crash site. we discussed the crash and collected additional photographs to aide us in reconstructing how the crash occurred. we believe that [person] walking (westbound) back towards his vehicle in [roadway] when he was struck by the f-150 truck as it was spinning on the ice. we believe that [person] over the top of the hood at an angle (center to driver`s side) and was then propelled towards the green chevy truck when the drives side rear quarter panel of the f-150 rotated around in the spin and contacted him again. there is an indention on the hood of the f-150 that is consistent with that of a body (slap) and direction of force for this crash. in addition there are heat transfer marks on the driver side rear quarter panel and tire of the truck that would be consistent with secondary contact with the victim as the truck was spinning. we believe the secondary contact shoved the victim towards the green chevy truck where he hit his head on the lower front left (driver`s side) of the bumper before coming to rest under the front axle. photographic evidence of the front bumper from the [medical facility] support the above statements. the f-150 then crashed nose first into the driver`s side of the saturn and both vehicles slid into the green chevrolet truck. after impacting the chevy, the f-150 broke away and came to rest west of the crash site and the saturn (slapped) off the chevy and wound up east of the crash site. we believe that as the saturn passed by the chevy truck, it ran over [person]`s right foot which was protruding out from underneath the front of the chevy truck. photographic evidence appears to indicate that [person]`s right foot is broken and photographs taken of his right boot show evidence of having been run over. there are ridges on the back of the ankle that appear to have been flattened/pushed down as compared to the left boot. after reviewing all the evidence and circumstances involved with this crash, the little elm police department accident investigation/reconstruction team concluded that no criminal actions attributed to the crash and no criminal charges will be filed.
